definition_zh: 消化的；助消化的；（英式）消化饼干；助消化药
definition_en: relating to the process of digesting food, or helping that process
core_image: 一条从口到肛门的管道，沿途有胃、小肠等器官在分解食物
scene: 把镜头拉近到这样一个场景：The doctor asked about his digestive symptoms after the meal.
sceneCN: 这里 digestive 指「消化系统的」（第 3 个义项：与消化道及其功能相关）；句意：医生询问他饭后出现的消化道症状。图中可辨识物件：人体消化道示意图、胃、小肠、病历问诊表。

pos.zh: 消化的；助消化的；消化系统的
（英式）消化饼干（digestive biscuit 的简称）；助消化药

senses.title: Relating to digestion
senses.titleCN: 消化的：与消化过程有关
senses.definition: connected with the process by which food is broken down in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与食物在体内被分解的过程有关的
senses.example: Digestive processes begin before you swallow.
senses.exampleCN: 消化过程在你吞咽之前就开始了。
senses.why: Latin digestivus meant 'tending to break down', so the adjective starts as a description of the action itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 digestivus 意为「有分解倾向的」，因此这个形容词起初描述的就是动作本身。

senses.title: Helping digestion
senses.titleCN: 助消化的：帮助食物分解
senses.definition: describes a substance or drink that is thought to help the stomach work
senses.definitionCN: 形容被认为有助于胃部工作的物质或饮品
senses.example: A digestive herbal tea is sold after heavy meals.
senses.exampleCN: 大餐之后会售卖助消化的草本茶。
senses.why: The suffix -ive often marks a function, so the adjective came to mean 'serving digestion' as well as 'of digestion'.
senses.whyCN: -ive 后缀常标示功能，因此这个形容词除了「消化的」，也发展出「有助于消化的」义。

senses.title: Of the digestive system
senses.titleCN: 消化系统的：属于消化道及器官
senses.definition: belonging to the organs and tube that carry food through the body
senses.definitionCN: 属于把食物输送过身体的器官与管道
senses.example: The doctor asked about his digestive symptoms after the meal.
senses.exampleCN: 医生询问他饭后出现的消化道症状。
senses.why: Anatomy needed a compact adjective for the whole tract, and this was the readiest one.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学需要为整条消化道找一个简洁的形容词，这个词最顺手。

senses.title: Of digestive organs
senses.titleCN: 消化器官的：胃、肠、肝、胰等
senses.definition: describes the organs themselves, such as the stomach, intestines, liver and pancreas
senses.definitionCN: 形容胃、肠、肝、胰等器官本身
senses.example: The digestive organs receive about a quarter of the blood flow.
senses.exampleCN: 消化器官接受约四分之一的血流量。
senses.why: The same adjective shifts from the process to the body parts that carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词从过程转指执行该过程的身体部件。

senses.title: Of juices and enzymes
senses.definition: describes the fluids and enzymes released into the gut to split food
senses.definitionCN: 形容释放到肠道中、用于分解食物的液体与酶
senses.example: Digestive juices are alkaline in the small intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 小肠里的消化液呈碱性。
senses.why: Once the chemistry of digestion was understood, the adjective attached naturally to the agents that do the splitting.
senses.whyCN: 消化的化学机制被理解之后，这个形容词自然附着在完成分解的介质上。

senses.title: Digestive biscuit
senses.titleCN: 消化饼干：英式名称，并非真的助消化
senses.definition: in British usage, a semi-sweet biscuit originally marketed as a digestive aid
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法，指一种半甜饼干，最初以助消化为卖点
senses.example: She had two digestives with her tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她喝茶时吃了两块消化饼干。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century bakers used the word as a health claim, and the name outlived the claim as a product label.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪烘焙商把这个词当作健康卖点，饼干名却比这个声称活得更久，成了产品标签。

senses.title: Digestive health
senses.titleCN: 消化健康：肠道功能的整体状态
senses.definition: in health writing, the general condition of the gut, including comfort and regularity
senses.definitionCN: 在健康写作中指肠道的整体状况，包括舒适与规律
senses.example: Fibre is central to digestive health.
senses.exampleCN: 膳食纤维对消化健康至关重要。
senses.why: Modern wellness language made 'digestive' a label for a whole domain of wellbeing, not only for an organ.
senses.whyCN: 现代健康语汇把 digestive 变成一个整体健康领域的标签，而不再只指某个器官。

senses.title: A digestive remedy
senses.titleCN: 助消化药：用于缓解肠胃不适的制剂
senses.definition: as a countable noun, a preparation taken to relieve stomach trouble
senses.definitionCN: 作可数名词，指用于缓解肠胃不适的制剂
senses.example: The pharmacist recommended a digestive for bloating.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师推荐了一种缓解腹胀的助消化药。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for a product that embodies the quality, as with a 'sedative' or an 'aperient'.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词转成名词，指体现该性质的产品，如 sedative、aperient。

intro.en: Digestive is the Latin adjective digestivus, built on digestus, the past participle of digerere 'to carry apart'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: digestive 是拉丁形容词 digestivus，由 digerere「分开搬运」的过去分词 digestus 构成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Digestus, the past participle of digerere, meant 'separated, distributed, arranged'. The adjective digestivus was formed on it with -ivus 'tending to'.
items.cn: digestus 是 digerere 的过去分词，意为「被分开、被分配、被整理」。形容词 digestivus 由它加 -ivus「有……倾向」构成。

items.en: Medieval medical Latin used digestivus for things that promote or belong to the processing of food; the word stayed close to the action rather than to an organ.
items.cn: 中世纪医学拉丁用 digestivus 指促进食物加工或与之相关的事物；这个词始终贴近动作，而不是某个器官。

items.en: English digestive appears in the fourteenth century, first as an adjective of the process and soon also of the organs.
items.cn: 英语 digestive 于 14 世纪出现，最初是过程形容词，很快也用于器官。

items.en: In the nineteenth century British bakers used 'digestive' in a health claim for a mildly sweet biscuit; the name survives although the claim does not.
items.cn: 19 世纪英国烘焙商把 digestive 用作一种微甜饼干的健康卖点；声称早已不再，名称却保留下来。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation and the date when the biscuit name was coined are both uncertain; the deeper root of digerere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与饼干命名年代）：英语最早书证与饼干名称出现的年代均存疑；digerere 的更深词根属重构形式。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family or the same spelling area; the second holds near-synonyms that name the gut and its workings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族或拼写相近的词；第二组是命名肠道及其运作的近义词。

entries.definition: The process itself; the adjective describes what belongs to that process.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；形容词则描述属于该过程的事物。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to break food down or absorb ideas; it names the action, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指分解食物或吸收观点；它命名动作，而非性质。

entries.definition: A property of food, meaning it can be digested; digestive describes the machinery or the process.
entries.definitionCN: 食物的属性，意为可被消化；digestive 描述机制或过程。

entries.definition: An uncommon adjective meaning 'not promoting digestion' or 'suffering poor digestion'
entries.definitionCN: 罕用形容词，意为「不利于消化的」或「消化不佳的」。

entries.definition: The technical adjective for the stomach and intestines; it is more formal and more precise than digestive.
entries.definitionCN: 指胃与肠的专业形容词，比 digestive 更正式、更精确。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to the intestines, whereas digestive covers mouth to anus.
entries.definitionCN: 专指肠道，而 digestive 覆盖从口到肛门。

entries.definition: Relating only to the stomach; it is narrower than digestive.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指胃部，比 digestive 范围窄。

entries.definition: Relating to food and the tube that carries it, as in alimentary canal; it stresses nourishment rather than breakdown.
entries.definitionCN: 指食物及输送食物的管道，如消化道；它强调滋养而非分解。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: digest + -ive 'tending to': the adjective of the breaking-down action.
normal.cn: digest + -ive「有……倾向」：分解动作的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs digest, digestion, digestible, indigestion and digestibility.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 digest、digestion、digestible、indigestion、digestibility。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: digestive system, digestive tract, digestive enzyme, digestive health.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖结构：消化系统、消化道、消化酶、消化健康。

normal.en: A digestive biscuit is a British product name, not a medicine.
normal.cn: digestive biscuit 是英国产品名，并不是药。

normal.en: gastrointestinal and gastric are the narrower clinical words.
normal.cn: gastrointestinal 与 gastric 是范围更窄的临床用词。

abstract.en: Picture a tube from mouth to anus, with several rooms opening off it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从口到肛门的管道，旁边开着几个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of dark tea and a round biscuit on a saucer after a heavy dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿饱餐之后，茶托上放着深色茶与一块圆饼干。

abstract.en: Picture a small bottle of pills labelled for stomach discomfort in an old pharmacy.
abstract.cn: 想象旧药房里一只小药瓶，标签上写着缓解肠胃不适。

examples.en: The digestive tract is about nine metres long in an adult.
examples.cn: 成年人的消化道长约九米。

examples.en: Digestive enzymes in the small intestine finish most chemical breakdown.
examples.cn: 小肠中的消化酶完成了大部分化学分解。

examples.en: He bought a packet of digestives for the train journey.
examples.cn: 他买了一包消化饼干带上火车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「digest 消化 + ive 的」——与消化有关的 → digestive 消化的

root: 拉丁 digerere「分开搬运」→ digestus「被分解的」→ 拉丁形容词 digestivus → 英语 digestive。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: the adjective of breaking food down attaches to the process, to the organs, to the juices, to a product label, and finally to a whole domain of health.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：分解食物的形容词先附着于过程，再附着于器官、消化液、产品标签，最后附着于一个完整的健康领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tube from mouth to anus, lined with rooms where food is split.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从口到肛门的管道，沿途有几个把食物拆开的房间。

branches.en: ACTION AND AID: the adjective can describe the breakdown itself or a substance meant to help it.
branches.cn: 动作与助力：这个形容词既可描述分解本身，也可描述用来帮助分解的东西。

branches.en: THE TUBE AND ITS ROOMS: from the whole tract the word narrows to the stomach, intestines, liver and pancreas.
branches.cn: 管道与房间：从整条消化道收窄到胃、肠、肝、胰。

branches.en: THE AGENTS: juices and enzymes are the chemical hands that do the splitting.
branches.cn: 执行者：消化液与酶是完成分解的化学之手。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT SHELF: a biscuit carries the name as marketing, and a remedy carries it as a promise of relief.
branches.cn: 产品货架：饼干把这个名字当营销，药品则把它当成缓解的承诺。

branches.en: THE WHOLE DOMAIN: modern health writing uses the word for the general condition of the gut.
branches.cn: 整个领域：现代健康写作把这个词用于肠道的整体状况。

intro.en: Digestive is a Latin participle stem plus the adjective suffix -ive: digest- + -ive.
intro.cn: digestive 是拉丁分词词干加形容词后缀 -ive：digest- + -ive。

latinIntro.en: Latin digerere 'to carry apart' gives digestus and digestivus; English builds digest, digestion, digestible, indigestion and digestibility on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 digerere「分开搬运」产生 digestus 与 digestivus；英语在同一词干上构造 digest、digestion、digestible、indigestion、digestibility。

items.meaningCN: 与消化有关或有助于消化的
items.example: The digestive system includes the liver and pancreas.

items.meaning: the process of breaking down food
to break food down; to absorb ideas
items.example: It takes hours to digest a heavy meal.
items.exampleCN: 消化一顿饱餐需要数小时。

items.example: Raw cellulose is indigestible to humans.
items.exampleCN: 生纤维素人体无法消化。
辛辣食物让他消化不良。

items.example: Breeders select for digestibility in forage grass.
items.exampleCN: 育种者会筛选牧草的可消化性。
这两餐在消化方面有所不同。

definition_zh: 数字的；数码的；手指的
definition_en: using numbers stored as electronic signals, especially in computers
core_image: 一块屏幕亮起，无数小方格排成图案，每个格子只有亮与不亮
scene: 老人把胶片相机收进抽屉，换了一台薄薄的机器。All the photos are now stored in digital form.
sceneCN: 这里 digital 指「数字的」（第 1 个义项：以数字信号记录）；句意是如今所有照片都以数字形式保存。

senses.title: Stored as numbers
senses.definition: recorded as a series of numbers that a machine can read
senses.definitionCN: 被记录成一串机器能读的数字
senses.example: The signal is converted into digital form.
senses.exampleCN: 信号被转换成数字形式。
senses.why: A smooth wave is cut into steps that a chip can count.
senses.whyCN: 平滑的波被切成格子，芯片才数得清。

senses.title: Built around such signals
senses.definition: describing devices and services that work with such signals
senses.definitionCN: 形容依靠这类信号运转的设备与服务
senses.example: The digital camera fits in a coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 这台数码相机能塞进外套口袋。
senses.why: The product is named after the kind of signal inside it.
senses.whyCN: 产品是照着它内部那种信号来命名的。

senses.title: Relating to a finger
senses.definition: relating to a finger or a toe in medical use
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指与手指或脚趾有关
senses.example: The surgeon repaired a digital nerve.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生修复了一根手指神经。
senses.why: The oldest sense comes from counting on the fingers.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的那层意思，来自扳着手指计数。

intro.en: Digital comes from Latin digitus, a finger, because people once counted on their fingers.
intro.cn: digital 来自拉丁语 digitus（手指），因为人最早是扳着手指计数的。

items.en: Digitus meant a finger or a toe.
items.cn: digitus 指手指或脚趾。

items.en: The same word named a numeral, since fingers were the first counters.
items.cn: 同一个词也指数目，因为手指是最早的算具。

items.en: English digit meant a number below ten.
items.cn: 英语 digit 指十以下的数字。

items.en: Digital described anything done with a finger.
items.cn: digital 形容任何用手指完成的事。

items.en: Electronics gave the word its current sense of number-coded signals.
items.cn: 电子技术让它有了今天「数字编码信号」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the digit- stem, while the meaning group covers numbers, electronics and two-state coding.
note.cn: 形近组共用 digit 词干，近义组则覆盖数值、电子与两态编码。

entries.definition: one of the numbers from zero to nine
entries.definitionCN: 零到九中的一个数字

entries.definition: the quality of deserving respect
entries.definitionCN: 值得尊重的品质

entries.definition: to turn information into numbers
entries.definitionCN: 把信息转换成数字

entries.definition: expressed by numbers
entries.definitionCN: 用数字表示的

entries.definition: working with tiny electric circuits
entries.definitionCN: 靠微型电路工作的

entries.definition: using only two states, such as on and off
entries.definitionCN: 只用通与断这两种状态的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with fingers used for counting and end with a screen of on and off cells.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从数数的手指开始，最后落到一块只有亮与不亮的屏幕。

normal.en: Digit is a finger first and a number second.
normal.cn: digit 先是手指，后才是数字。

normal.en: Ten fingers gave us ten digits, and digits gave us digital.
normal.cn: 十根手指给出十个数字，数字又给出 digital。

normal.en: Digital sound is a wave cut into tiny stairs.
normal.cn: 数字声音是被切成小台阶的波。

normal.en: A digital photo is a grid of numbers pretending to be light.
normal.cn: 数码照片是一格数字假装成光。

normal.en: Before screens, digital meant done with a finger.
normal.cn: 在有屏幕之前，digital 只表示用手指做的事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding up three fingers to count.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起三根手指在数数。

abstract.en: Picture a waveform chopped into equal steps.
abstract.cn: 想象一条波形被切成等高的台阶。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of cells where each is either lit or dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一片方格，每一格要么亮，要么暗。

examples.en: Most music is now sold in digital form.
examples.cn: 如今大多数音乐以数字形式出售。

examples.en: The digital clock lost a minute every month.
examples.cn: 这台数字钟每个月慢一分钟。

examples.en: Older workers often fear the digital age.
examples.cn: 年长的工人常常害怕数字时代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 digital 记成「地记头」：地上一格一格记下来，数字排好，就是数码。

root: 来自拉丁语 digitus（手指）。人最早扳手指计数，所以同一个词也指数目，英语 digit 便指零到九的数字。二十世纪电子技术用「只有通与断两种状态」的方式记录信息，digital 因此获得今天「数字的、数码的」这层含义，而医学上仍保留「手指的」原义。

sensesIntro.en: From counting on fingers, to a signal counted by a chip, to the devices built on that signal, and back to the finger itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从扳手指计数，到芯片数得出的信号，到靠这种信号运转的设备，最后回到手指本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grid of cells, each either lit or dark, forming a picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片方格，每格或亮或暗，凑成一幅图。

chain: A CHIP READS ON AND OFF

branches.en: The first sense is the coded signal itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那串被编码的信号。

branches.en: The second sense names the machines built on it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项指靠它运转的机器。

branches.en: The third sense returns to the body part.
branches.cn: 第三个义项回到身体部位。

branches.en: The signal and the device share one adjective.
branches.cn: 信号与设备共用同一个形容词。

branches.en: The newest sense and the oldest both trace back to fingers.
branches.cn: 最新的意思与最老的意思，都能追回到手指。

intro.en: Digital belongs to the digit- family, running from fingers to numbers to machine code.
intro.cn: digital 属于 digit 一族，从手指一路走到数字，再到机器编码。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin digitus, a finger, which also gave the word for a numeral.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 digitus（手指），它同时给出了「数字」这个词。

items.exampleCN: 这批档案已全部数字化。

items.example: Write the answer as a single digit.
The form can be signed digitally.
They digitize old tapes each winter.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年冬天把旧磁带数字化。

items.meaning: the act of converting to numbers
items.exampleCN: 数字化抢救了那些易碎的地图。
数字化改变了整个办公室。

items.meaning: a plant named for its finger-shaped flowers
items.example: Digitalis is used in small doses.
items.exampleCN: 毛地黄只以小剂量入药。

definition_zh: v. 使显得高贵；使尊荣；抬高…的身价；给…冠以美名（常含讽刺）
definition_en: to make something seem worthy or noble, often used ironically for giving undeserved standing
core_image: 一块素布铺上旧木桌，桌面立刻显得体面；另一头，一条匿名谣言被手指悬在屏幕上方，终究没有点下去
scene: 别用回应去抬高那条谣言。Do not dignify the rumour with a reply.
sceneCN: 这里 dignify 是讽刺用法（第 2 个义项：给不值得的东西加上体面的名分）；句意是别用回应去抬高那条谣言。图中可辨识物件：手机上的匿名留言、悬在屏幕上方却不点下去的手指、旁边的删除图标。

pos.zh: 使显得高贵；使尊荣；抬高…的身价；给…冠以美名

senses.title: Lend dignity to
senses.definition: to give an ordinary thing a calm, worthy appearance
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让平常的东西显得沉着而体面
senses.example: A plain cloth dignifies the old table.
senses.exampleCN: 一块素布让旧桌子显得体面。
senses.why: A bare wooden table covered with one folded linen cloth.
senses.whyCN: 一张裸木桌铺上一块折好的亚麻布。

senses.title: Give false grandeur
senses.definition: to treat something unworthy as if it deserved attention
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把不值得的东西当成值得关注的来对待
senses.example: Do not dignify the rumour with a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 别用回应去抬高那条谣言。
senses.why: A finger hovering over an anonymous message without tapping it.
senses.whyCN: 一根手指悬在匿名留言上方却不点下去。

senses.title: Raise in rank
senses.definition: to honour someone with a title or higher standing
senses.definitionCN: （动词）用头衔或更高的身份来尊荣某人
senses.example: The charter dignified the guild with new rights.
senses.exampleCN: 那份特许状授予行会新的权利，使其显贵。
senses.why: A sealed charter handed to a merchant across a counter.
senses.whyCN: 一份盖印的特许状隔着柜台递给商人。

intro.en: Dignify comes from Latin dignus, worthy, through dignitas and late Latin dignificare, to make worthy.
intro.cn: dignify 来自拉丁语 dignus（值得的），经 dignitas 与晚期拉丁语 dignificare（使值得）而来。

items.en: Dignus meant worthy or deserving.
items.cn: dignus 意为值得的、相称的。

items.en: Dignitas named worth and standing.
items.cn: dignitas 指价值与身份。

items.en: Dignificare meant to make worthy.
items.cn: dignificare 意为使变得值得。

items.en: Old French carried the verb north.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带到北方。

items.en: Dignify entered English for honouring something.
items.cn: 十五世纪 dignify 以「使尊荣」义进入英语。

items.en: Today it often refuses honour instead of giving it.
items.cn: 如今它常用于拒绝给予体面。

note.en: The look-alike group is the dign- worthy family; the near-meaning group names other ways of raising something up.
note.cn: 形近组是 dign-（值得）家族；近义组是其他表示「抬高」的词。

entries.definition: Worth and calm self-respect.
entries.definitionCN: 价值与沉着的自尊。

entries.definition: Calm and worthy of respect.
entries.definitionCN: 沉着而值得尊敬。

entries.definition: Angry at something unfair.
entries.definitionCN: 对不公之事感到愤怒。

entries.definition: To make noble in rank or character.
entries.definitionCN: 使在身份或品格上高贵。

entries.definition: To raise in rank or level.
entries.definitionCN: 提升身份或水平。

entries.definition: To make something seem splendid, often falsely.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物显得辉煌，常属虚美。

normalIntro.en: Dignify is dign- worthy plus -ify make: lend something a worth it may not have earned.
normalIntro.cn: dignify 就是 dign-（值得）加 -ify（使）：把体面借给某样也许并不配的东西。

normal.en: Dign- worthy plus -ify make means make it worthy.
normal.cn: dign-（值得）加 -ify（使）就是使它显得值得。

normal.en: Dignity is the noun, dignified the adjective.
normal.cn: dignity 是名词，dignified 是形容词。

normal.en: It is often ironic: refuse to dignify a rumour.
normal.cn: 它常带讽刺：拒绝用回应抬高谣言。

normal.en: Indignant is the angry cousin from the same root.
normal.cn: indignant 是同根的愤怒表亲。

normal.en: Dignify can also mean grant a title.
normal.cn: dignify 也可指授予头衔。

abstract.en: A bare wooden table covered with one folded linen cloth.
abstract.cn: 一张裸木桌铺上一块折好的亚麻布。

abstract.en: A finger hovering over an anonymous message without tapping it.
abstract.cn: 一根手指悬在匿名留言上方却不点下去。

abstract.en: A sealed charter handed to a merchant across a counter.
abstract.cn: 一份盖印的特许状隔着柜台递给商人。

examples.en: A plain cloth dignifies the old table.
examples.cn: 一块素布让旧桌子显得体面。

examples.en: She would not dignify the insult with an answer.
examples.cn: 她不愿用回答去抬高那句侮辱。

examples.en: The charter dignified the guild with new rights.
examples.cn: 那份特许状授予行会新的权利，使其显贵。

dict_mnemonic.text: dignify ＝ dign-（拉丁语 dignus「值得的」，同根 dignity、dignified）＋ -ify（使…）＝「使显得值得、使高贵」。现代英语最常见的是讽刺用法：别用回应去抬高一条谣言。

root: 拉丁语 dignus（值得的）→ dignitas（价值、身份）→ 晚期拉丁语 dignificare（使值得）→ 古法语 dignifier → 英语 dignify

sensesIntro.en: Worth lent outward: a cloth on a bare table, a reply withheld from a rumour and a title on a merchant.
sensesIntro.cn: 往外借出的体面：素布铺上裸桌、一句忍住了没给谣言的回应，以及加给商人的头衔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one folded linen cloth laid on a bare wooden table so the whole surface looks worthy
core.cn: 核心意象：一块折好的亚麻布铺上裸木桌，整个桌面就显得体面

branches.en: A bare wooden table covered with one folded linen cloth.
branches.cn: 一张裸木桌铺上一块折好的亚麻布。

branches.en: A finger hovering over an anonymous message without tapping it.
branches.cn: 一根手指悬在匿名留言上方却不点下去。

branches.en: A sealed charter handed to a merchant across a counter.
branches.cn: 一份盖印的特许状隔着柜台递给商人。

branches.en: Both hand out a worth that was not there before.
branches.cn: 两者都把原先没有的体面递出去。

branches.en: Both turn on whether the standing is deserved.
branches.cn: 两者都取决于这份身份是否配得上。

intro.en: Dignify is dign- plus -ify; the worthy root also builds dignity, dignitary and indignant.
intro.cn: dignify 由 dign- 加 -ify 构成；值得这个词根也造出 dignity、dignitary 与 indignant。

latinIntro.en: Latin dignus means worthy, dignitas worth and standing, facere to make.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dignus 意为值得的，dignitas 意为价值与身份，facere 意为做、使。

definition_zh: v.（使）扩张；（使）膨胀；（瞳孔、血管）放大；详述（dilate on）
definition_en: to make or become wider or larger, especially an opening in the body; also to speak at length
core_image: 房间灯一暗，虹膜中央那个黑圆就慢慢张大；同一根管子在压力下向外鼓起来
scene: 瞳孔在暗处会放大。The pupils dilate in the dark.
sceneCN: 这里 dilate 是「（开口）扩张」（第 1 个义项：瞳孔、血管等开口变大）；句意是瞳孔在暗处会放大。图中可辨识物件：一只眼睛的特写、虹膜中央变大的黑圆、墙上的调光开关。

pos.zh: （使）扩张；（使）膨胀；（瞳孔、血管）放大；详述

senses.title: Widen an opening
senses.definition: of a pupil, vessel or passage, to become wider
senses.definitionCN: （动词）（瞳孔、血管或通道）变得更宽
senses.example: The pupils dilate in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 瞳孔在暗处会放大。
senses.why: A close-up iris whose black centre grows as the lamp dims.
senses.whyCN: 一只虹膜的特写，灯一暗中央的黑圆就变大。

senses.title: Swell in volume
senses.definition: to expand in bulk, as gas or metal does when heated
senses.definitionCN: （动词）体积变大，如气体或金属受热时
senses.example: The metal dilates as the furnace heats it.
senses.exampleCN: 炉子加热时金属会膨胀。
senses.why: A rod pushed against a gauge while its length creeps outward.
senses.whyCN: 一根杆顶着量规，长度慢慢往外爬。

senses.title: Speak at length
senses.definition: to write or speak about a subject in great detail
senses.definitionCN: （动词）非常详细地写或讲某个题目
senses.example: He dilated on the history of the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 他详述了那条运河的历史。
senses.why: A lecturer still at the same slide twenty minutes later.
senses.whyCN: 一位讲者二十分钟后还停在同一张幻灯片上。

intro.en: Dilate comes from Latin dilatare, from dis- apart and latus, wide; it is not related to dilatory, which comes from differre.
intro.cn: dilate 来自拉丁语 dilatare，由 dis-（分开）与 latus（宽的）构成；它与 dilatory 无关，后者来自 differre。

items.en: Latus meant wide or broad.
items.cn: latus 意为宽的、宽阔的。

items.en: Dis- meant apart.
items.cn: dis- 意为分开。

items.en: Dilatare meant to spread wider.
items.cn: dilatare 意为撑得更宽。

items.en: Old French passed the verb on.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词传了下来。

items.en: Dilate entered English for widening.
items.cn: 十五世纪 dilate 以「变宽」义进入英语。

items.en: Doctors used it for pupils and vessels.
items.cn: 医生用它描述瞳孔与血管。

note.en: The look-alike group hides two false friends, dilution and dilatory; the near-meaning group names plain widening.
note.cn: 形近组藏着 dilution 与 dilatory 两个形近陷阱；近义组是直白的「变宽」。

entries.definition: Making a liquid weaker, from luere to wash, not latus wide.
entries.definitionCN: 使液体变淡；源自 luere（洗），不是 latus（宽）。

entries.definition: Tending to delay; from differre, not from dilatare.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于拖延；来自 differre，不是 dilatare。

entries.definition: The act or state of widening.
entries.definitionCN: 变宽这一动作或状态。

entries.definition: To become larger in size or scope.
entries.definitionCN: 在体积或范围上变大。

entries.definition: To make or become wider.
entries.definitionCN: 使变宽或变宽。

entries.definition: To swell from internal pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 因内部压力而膨胀。

normalIntro.en: Dilate is dis- apart plus lat- wide: an opening pushed wider, and dilatory is only a look-alike.
normalIntro.cn: dilate 就是 dis-（分开）加 lat-（宽）：一个被撑宽的开口；dilatory 只是形近。

normal.en: Dis- apart plus lat- wide means spread it wide.
normal.cn: dis-（分开）加 lat-（宽）就是撑宽。

normal.en: Pupils dilate when the light goes down.
normal.cn: 光线变暗时瞳孔会放大。

normal.en: Dilation is the noun doctors use.
normal.cn: dilation 是医生用的名词。

normal.en: Dilatory looks close but means delaying.
normal.cn: dilatory 形近，却是「拖延的」。

normal.en: To dilate on a subject is to speak at length.
normal.cn: dilate on 一个话题就是详细展开讲。

abstract.en: A close-up iris whose black centre grows as the lamp dims.
abstract.cn: 一只虹膜的特写，灯一暗中央的黑圆就变大。

abstract.en: A rod pushed against a gauge while its length creeps outward.
abstract.cn: 一根杆顶着量规，长度慢慢往外爬。

abstract.en: A lecturer still at the same slide twenty minutes later.
abstract.cn: 一位讲者二十分钟后还停在同一张幻灯片上。

examples.en: The pupils dilate in the dark.
examples.cn: 瞳孔在暗处会放大。

examples.en: The drug dilates the coronary arteries.
examples.cn: 这种药会扩张冠状动脉。

examples.en: He dilated on the history of the canal.
examples.cn: 他详述了那条运河的历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: dilate ＝ di-（＝dis-，分开）＋ lat-（拉丁语 latus「宽」，同根 latitude）＋ -ate（动词后缀）＝「撑宽、扩张」；医学里说瞳孔、血管 dilate。注意 dilatory（拖延的）来自 differre，是形近陷阱。

root: 拉丁语 dis-（分开）＋ latus（宽的）→ dilatare（撑宽）→ 古法语 dilater → 英语 dilate

sensesIntro.en: An opening that grows: a black circle in the iris, a rod against a gauge and a speaker who will not stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个变大的开口：虹膜里的黑圆、顶着量规的杆，以及一位停不下来的讲者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the black circle at the centre of an iris widening as the room light is turned down
core.cn: 核心意象：房间灯被调暗时，虹膜中央的黑圆慢慢张大

branches.en: A close-up iris whose black centre grows as the lamp dims.
branches.cn: 一只虹膜的特写，灯一暗中央的黑圆就变大。

branches.en: A rod pushed against a gauge while its length creeps outward.
branches.cn: 一根杆顶着量规，长度慢慢往外爬。

branches.en: A lecturer still at the same slide twenty minutes later.
branches.cn: 一位讲者二十分钟后还停在同一张幻灯片上。

branches.en: Both take up more room than before.
branches.cn: 两者都比原先占据更多空间。

branches.en: Both stretch something past its usual limit.
branches.cn: 两者都把某样东西撑过平常的限度。

intro.en: Dilate is di- plus lat- plus -ate; the wide root also gives latitude, while expand and distend use other roots.
intro.cn: dilate 由 di- 加 lat- 加 -ate 构成；宽这个词根也给出 latitude，而 expand 与 distend 用的是别的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin latus means wide, dilatare to widen and tendere to stretch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 latus 意为宽的，dilatare 意为撑宽，tendere 意为伸展。

definition_zh: n. 困境；两难；进退维谷；（逻辑）二难推理
definition_en: a situation in which a choice must be made between two options that both carry a cost
core_image: 岔路口一块双向指路牌，两条小径都通向麻烦；一双鞋停在原地不动
scene: 两条路都不好走，他站在岔口。He faced a real dilemma at the fork.
sceneCN: 这里 dilemma 是「两难选择」（第 1 个义项：两个选项都有明显代价）；句意是他在岔路口面临真正的两难。图中可辨识物件：岔路口的两条小径、一块双向指路牌、停在原地的一双鞋。

pos.zh: 困境；两难；进退维谷；（逻辑）二难推理

senses.title: Two costly options
senses.definition: a choice between two options that both carry a clear cost
senses.definitionCN: （名词）两个选项都带明显代价的选择
senses.example: He faced a real dilemma at the fork.
senses.exampleCN: 他在岔路口面临真正的两难。
senses.why: A signpost with two arrows and a pair of shoes standing still.
senses.whyCN: 一块有两个箭头的指路牌，旁边一双鞋站着不动。

senses.title: Any hard predicament
senses.definition: a difficult situation with no easy way out
senses.definitionCN: （名词）没有轻松出路的困难处境
senses.example: The funding cut left the clinic in a dilemma.
senses.exampleCN: 经费削减让诊所陷入困境。
senses.why: A clinic calendar with half its slots crossed out.
senses.whyCN: 一本诊所日程表，一半的时段被划掉。

senses.title: A logical double bind
senses.definition: an argument forcing a choice between two premises with the same bad result
senses.definitionCN: （名词）迫使人在两个前提间选择、而结果同样糟糕的论证
senses.example: The speaker built a dilemma from two premises.
senses.exampleCN: 讲者用两个前提构造了一个二难推理。
senses.why: Two arrows on a board converging on one boxed conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 白板上两个箭头汇聚到同一个方框结论。

intro.en: Dilemma is Greek di- twice plus lemma, a premise taken, from lambanein to take; it entered English as a debating trap.
intro.cn: dilemma 是希腊语 di-（二）加 lemma（拿来的前提），lemma 来自 lambanein（拿取）；它作为辩论中的夹击进入英语。

items.en: Di- meant twice.
items.cn: di- 意为两次。

items.en: Lambanein meant to take.
items.cn: lambanein 意为拿取。

items.en: Lemma named a premise taken for argument.
items.cn: lemma 指辩论中先拿来的前提。

items.en: Dilemma named a double premise that traps you.
items.cn: dilemma 指把你困住的双重前提。

items.en: English borrowed it as a debating trap.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语借入时指辩论中的夹击。

items.en: It now means any hard two-way choice.
items.cn: 如今它泛指任何艰难的二选一。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the lemma premise; the near-meaning group names other tight situations.
note.cn: 形近组共享 lemma（前提）；近义组是其他表示「处境艰难」的词。

entries.definition: A premise, or a proved helper theorem.
entries.definitionCN: 一个前提，或一条辅助定理。

entries.definition: A choice among three unwelcome options.
entries.definitionCN: 三个都不想要的选项之间的选择。

entries.definition: A dabbler in the arts; unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术上的浅尝者；词源无关。

entries.definition: An unpleasant situation hard to escape.
entries.definitionCN: 难以脱身的不快处境。

entries.definition: A state of not knowing what to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 不知如何决定的状态。

entries.definition: A situation with no way forward.
entries.definitionCN: 无路可走的局面。

normalIntro.en: Dilemma is di- two plus lemma premise: two premises closing on you like a pair of horns.
normalIntro.cn: dilemma 就是 di-（二）加 lemma（前提）：两个前提像一对牛角朝你合拢。

normal.en: Di- two plus lemma premise means two premises, both bad.
normal.cn: di-（二）加 lemma（前提）就是两个前提，都不好。

normal.en: A dilemma has horns: whichever you take, it hurts.
normal.cn: dilemma 有角：抓哪一头都疼。

normal.en: In logic it is a forced choice of arguments.
normal.cn: 在逻辑里它是被迫的二选一论证。

normal.en: A false dilemma pretends there are only two options.
normal.cn: 假两难假装只有两个选项。

normal.en: Trilemma is the three-way version.
normal.cn: trilemma 是三选一版本。

abstract.en: A signpost with two arrows and a pair of shoes standing still.
abstract.cn: 一块有两个箭头的指路牌，旁边一双鞋站着不动。

abstract.en: A clinic calendar with half its slots crossed out.
abstract.cn: 一本诊所日程表，一半的时段被划掉。

abstract.en: Two arrows on a board converging on one boxed conclusion.
abstract.cn: 白板上两个箭头汇聚到同一个方框结论。

examples.en: She faced a dilemma between duty and family.
examples.cn: 她在责任与家庭之间面临两难。

examples.en: The committee resolved the dilemma by splitting the budget.
examples.cn: 委员会通过拆分预算化解了这个困境。

examples.en: Offering only two options creates a false dilemma.
examples.cn: 只给两个选项就制造了假两难。

dict_mnemonic.text: dilemma ＝ di-（二）＋ lemma（希腊语「拿来的前提」，数学里的「引理」同词）＝两个前提把你夹住，「两难、困境」。想象牛的两个角：抓哪一头都疼。三选一叫 trilemma。

root: 希腊语 di-（二）＋ lemma（前提，来自 lambanein「拿取」）→ dilemma（双重前提的夹击）→ 拉丁语 dilemma → 英语 dilemma

sensesIntro.en: Two premises closing like horns: a fork in the path, a calendar half crossed out and a debater trapped.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个像牛角一样合拢的前提：岔路口、一本划掉一半的日程表，以及一个被夹住的辩手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signpost with two arrows at a fork while a pair of shoes stays planted between them
core.cn: 核心意象：岔路口一块有两个箭头的指路牌，一双鞋定在两条路之间不动

branches.en: A signpost with two arrows and a pair of shoes standing still.
branches.cn: 一块有两个箭头的指路牌，旁边一双鞋站着不动。

branches.en: A clinic calendar with half its slots crossed out.
branches.cn: 一本诊所日程表，一半的时段被划掉。

branches.en: Two arrows on a board converging on one boxed conclusion.
branches.cn: 白板上两个箭头汇聚到同一个方框结论。

branches.en: Both leave no comfortable way forward.
branches.cn: 两者都没有舒服的出路。

branches.en: Both close in from two sides at once.
branches.cn: 两者都从两侧同时合拢。

intro.en: Dilemma is di- plus lemma; the take root also builds syllable and synthesis, and tri- gives trilemma.
intro.cn: dilemma 由 di- 加 lemma 构成；拿取这个词根也造出 syllable 与 synthesis，tri- 则给出 trilemma。

latinIntro.en: Greek lambanein means to take and lemma a premise taken; Latin passus means a step.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 lambanein 意为拿取，lemma 意为拿来的前提；拉丁语 passus 意为一步。

definition_zh: n. 勤勉；勤奋；细致用心；（商务）尽职（due diligence）
definition_en: steady, careful and persistent effort in doing something
core_image: 台灯下摊开的练习册，草稿纸写满一张又一张；墙上的日历被一格格划掉
scene: 他靠勤勉补上了落下的功课。He caught up through sheer diligence.
sceneCN: 这里 diligence 是「勤勉」（第 1 个义项：长期、持续、用心地做事）；句意是他靠勤勉补上了落下的功课。图中可辨识物件：台灯下摊开的练习册、写满的草稿纸、墙上一格格划掉的日历。

pos.zh: 勤勉；勤奋；细致用心；（商务）尽职

senses.title: Steady careful effort
senses.definition: persistent, attentive work kept up over time
senses.definitionCN: （名词）长期保持的专注努力
senses.example: He caught up through sheer diligence.

items.en: Dis- meant apart.

definition_zh: 稀释；冲淡；削弱（效果、权力）；稀释过的
definition_en: to make a liquid weaker by adding water or another solvent, or to make something less forceful
core_image: 一小杯浓果汁倒进一大壶凉水，颜色从深褐立刻变浅
scene: 厨房里，服务员把一小杯浓缩果汁倒进一大壶凉水，颜色立刻从深褐变浅。The waiter diluted the strong juice with cold water before serving it.
sceneCN: 这里 dilute 指加水使浓度降低（第 1 个义项：稀释）；句意为服务员上桌前用凉水把浓果汁稀释。图中可辨识物件：浓缩果汁、水壶、玻璃杯、搅拌勺。

senses.title: To add water and lower concentration
senses.definition: to add water or another solvent to a liquid so that the amount of active substance in each unit falls
senses.definitionCN: 向液体中加入水或其他溶剂，使每单位中有效物质的量下降
senses.example: Dilute the acid with three parts water.
senses.exampleCN: 用三份水把这种酸稀释。
senses.why: dilute comes from Latin diluere 'to wash away', so the core action is washing strength out into a larger volume.
senses.whyCN: dilute 出自拉丁 diluere「冲走」，核心动作就是把强度冲散到更大的体积里。

senses.title: To weaken a solution before testing
senses.definition: to reduce the strength of a sample so that it falls within the range an instrument or a procedure can handle
senses.definitionCN: 降低样品的强度，使仪器或操作能处理
senses.example: The technician diluted the sample before testing.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员在检测前把样品稀释了。
senses.why: a sample that is too strong must be reduced, so laboratory routine turns the first sense into a standard step.
senses.whyCN: 过浓的样品必须减弱，实验室流程就把第一义变成标准步骤。

senses.title: To weaken power or influence
senses.definition: to make authority, influence or an advantage less effective by spreading it among more parties
senses.definitionCN: 把权威、影响力或优势分散给更多方，使其效力下降
senses.example: Adding more members diluted the chairman's influence.
senses.exampleCN: 增加成员削弱了主席的影响力。
senses.why: influence behaves like a solute: the same amount spread through more volume acts more weakly at any one point.
senses.whyCN: 影响力像溶质：同样的量摊进更大体积，在任一点上的作用就更弱。

senses.title: To weaken taste, colour or feeling
senses.definition: to make a quality fainter by mixing it with something neutral
senses.definitionCN: 通过与中性之物混合使某种性质变淡
senses.example: Too much water diluted the taste of the tea.
senses.exampleCN: 水太多，把茶味冲淡了。
senses.why: taste and colour are intensities carried in a liquid, so adding liquid lowers them just as it lowers concentration.
senses.whyCN: 味道与颜色是液体承载的强度，加水会像降低浓度一样把它们压低。

senses.title: Weakened by water, as an adjective
senses.titleCN: 形容词：稀释过的、浓度低的
senses.definition: having had water added, so that the substance is present at low strength
senses.definitionCN: 已加水，使物质以低强度存在
senses.example: A dilute solution of bleach is safe on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 稀释的漂白液用在地面上是安全的。
senses.why: the adjective is the same form, describing the state that the verb has produced.
senses.whyCN: 形容词是同一形式，描述动词造成的那种状态。

senses.title: To make a promise less forceful
senses.titleCN: 使承诺或主张变得无力
senses.definition: to take the force out of a statement, promise or claim by adding qualifications or compromises
senses.definitionCN: 通过附加条件或折中，抽掉陈述、承诺或主张的力量
senses.example: The final clause diluted the promise of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一条款把改革的承诺冲淡了。
senses.why: a claim is strong when nothing neutral is mixed in, so hedging works like adding water to a statement.
senses.whyCN: 主张在没有掺入中性成分时最强，因此含糊其辞就像给陈述加水。

senses.title: To reduce each shareholder's stake
senses.definition: to reduce the proportion of a company owned by existing shareholders by issuing more shares
senses.definitionCN: 通过发行更多股份，降低现有股东所占的公司比例
senses.example: Issuing new shares diluted existing holdings.
senses.exampleCN: 发行新股稀释了现有持股。
senses.why: ownership is a share of a fixed whole, so adding more shares spreads the same company over more claims.
senses.whyCN: 所有权是对一个固定整体的份额，增发股份就把同一家公司摊到更多索取权上。

senses.title: To spread intensity until it fades
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把强度摊到更大范围直至变淡
senses.definition: used figuratively of any intensity that loses force when spread over more time, space or recipients
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何强度因摊到更多时间、空间或对象而失去力量
senses.example: Praise repeated too often is diluted into noise.
senses.exampleCN: 赞美重复太多，就被冲淡成噪音。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the arithmetic of dilution: the same amount divided among more units counts for less in each.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了稀释的算术：同样的量分给更多单位，每一份就更少。

intro.en: Dilute comes from the Latin past participle dilutus, from diluere 'to wash away, dissolve, dilute', built on dis- 'apart' plus -luere, the combining form of lavere 'to wash'. It is recorded in English from the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dilute 来自拉丁过去分词 dilutus，出自 diluere「冲走、溶解、稀释」，由 dis-「分开」加 -luere 构成，后者是 lavere「洗」的组合形式。英语自十五世纪有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lavere meant 'to wash'; its combining form -luere appears in diluere and in words about flooding, and its older root is reconstructed as a verb of washing.
items.cn: lavere 意为「洗」，其组合形式 -luere 出现在 diluere 以及表示洪水的词中，其更古老词根被重构为一个表示「洗」的动词。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus -luere gave diluere 'to wash away, to dissolve, to dilute', the image being strength carried off into a larger body of water.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 -luere 构成 diluere「冲走、溶解、稀释」，画面是强度被带进更大一片水里。

items.en: The past participle dilutus 'washed away, diluted' is the direct source of the English adjective and of the verb built on it.
items.cn: 过去分词 dilutus「被冲走的、被稀释的」是英语形容词及由此构成的动词的直接来源。

items.en: From the fifteenth century English dilute meant to weaken a liquid by adding water, first in medicine and then in general use.
items.cn: 自十五世纪起，英语 dilute 指加水使液体变弱，先在医学中使用，后进入一般用法。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb described weakened power, claims and ownership, where the same arithmetic of spreading holds.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词已用于被削弱的权力、主张与所有权，因为「摊开」的算术是一样的。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of the washing root is a reconstruction, and its exact first English citation is not recorded. Note that this root is not the luere 'to loosen' behind soluble.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：表示「洗」的词根在拉丁语之前的形式属于重构，英语最早书证没有确切记录。需注意这个词根并非 soluble 背后表示「松开」的 luere。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes whose roots are different despite similar spelling; group two holds verbs for making something weaker.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近而词根不同的形近词；第二组是表示使某物变弱的动词。

entries.definition: The act or result of diluting; it is the noun built on this verb, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 稀释的动作或结果；由这个动词构成的名词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: To break a solid apart into a liquid; dilute does not dissolve anything, it only lowers the strength of what is already dissolved.
entries.definitionCN: 把固体拆散进液体；dilute 不溶解任何东西，只降低已溶解物的强度。

entries.definition: From Latin latus 'wide': to widen or expand, as a pupil or an artery does; it has nothing to do with washing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 latus「宽」：使变宽、扩张，如瞳孔或动脉；与「洗」无关。

entries.definition: From diluvium, a flood: water overwhelming everything, which is the violent version of the same washing image.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 diluvium「洪水」：水淹没一切，是同一「冲洗」意象的猛烈版本。

entries.definition: The broad verb for making anything less strong, with no image of water.
entries.definitionCN: 使任何事物变弱的通用动词，不含水的意象。

entries.definition: To make a liquid less thick, as paint with turpentine; it changes consistency rather than concentration.
entries.definitionCN: 使液体变稀薄，如用松节油调漆；改变的是稠度，而非浓度。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for adding water, and also for softening a statement; dilute is its formal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 加水的日常说法，也指软化表述；dilute 是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: To reduce the strength of a signal, a virus or a force; common in physics and medicine rather than in cookery.
entries.definitionCN: 降低信号、病毒或力量的强度；多用于物理与医学，而非厨房。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Diluere 'to wash away': water carries the strength off into a larger volume.
normal.cn: diluere「冲走」：水把强度带进更大的体积。

normal.en: The family runs dilute, dilution, diluent, diluted, undiluted.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dilute、dilution、diluent、diluted、undiluted。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the chemical sense: dilute acid, dilute a solution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出化学义：稀酸、稀释溶液。

normal.en: The figurative phrases mark the rest: dilute the effect, dilute ownership, dilute the message.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配标出其余义项：削弱效果、稀释所有权、冲淡信息。

normal.en: Remember the root is 'wash', not 'loosen': do not tie it to dissolve or soluble.
normal.cn: 记住词根是「洗」而不是「松开」：不要把它与 dissolve 或 soluble 系在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon of dark syrup turning a whole jug pale brown.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺深色糖浆把整壶水染成浅褐。

abstract.en: Picture applause spread thin over an hour until it sounds like background noise.
abstract.cn: 想象掌声摊薄在一小时里，最后听起来像背景噪音。

abstract.en: Picture one strong voice split among a hundred speakers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个洪亮的声音被分给一百个人。

examples.en: Always dilute the cleaning fluid before pouring it down the drain.
examples.cn: 把清洁液倒进排水口前一定要先稀释。

examples.en: The new partners diluted the founder's share to less than half.
examples.cn: 新合伙人把创始人的股份稀释到不足一半。

examples.en: Repeating the slogan at every stop diluted its effect.
examples.cn: 每到一站都重复这句口号，反而削弱了它的效果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「di（分开）+ lute（冲）」——把浓的冲散开：稀释、冲淡、削弱

root: 拉丁 diluere「冲走、稀释」的过去分词 dilutus = dis-（分开）+ -luere（洗，源自 lavere「洗」）；与 soluble 背后表示「松开」的 luere 并非同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one washing away: water lowers a concentration, a sample is made testable, power is spread thin, taste and colour fade, the adjective names the weakened state, a promise loses force, shares are spread over more owners, and finally any intensity fades as it is divided.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「冲走」：水降低浓度，样品被调到可测，权力被摊薄，味道与颜色变淡，形容词命名被削弱的状态，承诺失去力量，股份被摊到更多持有人，最后任何强度都因被分割而变淡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cup of dark juice poured into a large jug of clear water until the colour turns pale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小杯深色果汁倒进一大壶清水，颜色直到变浅。

branches.en: LOWERING STRENGTH: domestic dilution and laboratory dilution are one act at two scales.
branches.cn: 降低强度：日常稀释与实验室稀释，是同一动作的两个尺度。

branches.en: SPREAD AMONG MORE HOLDERS: influence and shares both lose force when divided among more parties.
branches.cn: 摊给更多持有者：影响力与股份一旦分给更多方，都会失去力量。

branches.en: FAINT QUALITIES: taste, colour and the force of a promise all fade when something neutral is mixed in.
branches.cn: 变淡的性质：味道、颜色与承诺的力量，都会因掺入中性之物而减退。

branches.en: THE WEAKENED STATE: the adjective simply names what the verb has already done.
branches.cn: 被削弱的状态：形容词只是命名动词已经做成的事。

branches.en: DIVIDED INTENSITY: any strength spread over more time or recipients counts for less at each point.
branches.cn: 被分割的强度：任何强度摊到更多时间或对象上，每一点的分量都更少。

intro.en: Dilute is a Latin verb made of a prefix and a root of washing, and the same pieces build the rest of its family.
intro.cn: dilute 是一个由前缀与「洗」词根构成的拉丁动词，同样的部分构成它其余的家族。

latinIntro.en: Dis- 'apart' plus -luere 'to wash' gives diluere and its participle dilutus; the same washing root appears in deluge and diluvial, not in dissolve.
latinIntro.cn: dis-「分开」加 -luere「洗」构成 diluere 及其分词 dilutus；同一「洗」词根出现在 deluge 与 diluvial 中，而不在 dissolve 中。

items.example: The prefix sends the strength away into the water.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把强度送进水里。

items.example: The root supplies the washing image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「洗」的意象。

items.example: Only the combining form appears inside diluere.
items.exampleCN: 在 diluere 内部只出现组合形式。

items.example: The Latin verb begins the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词开启词族。

items.example: Dilute the paint before the second coat.

items.meaning: the act or result of diluting
items.example: Two dilutions brought the sample into range.
items.exampleCN: 两次稀释把样品调进了量程。

items.example: Water is the cheapest diluent here.
items.exampleCN: 水是这里最便宜的稀释剂。

items.example: The diluted bleach was safe to use.
items.exampleCN: 稀释过的漂白液可以安全使用。
他没兑水就把果汁喝了。

items.example: The storm brought a deluge to the valley.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨给山谷带来一场洪水。

definition_zh: 尺寸；维度；方面；规模
definition_en: a measurement of length, width or height, or one part of a situation
core_image: 一只木箱被卷尺量过三次，长、宽、高各贴一张小纸条
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉开，沿箱子的三条边各量一次。The room's dimensions are printed on the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 dimensions 指「尺寸」（第 1 个义项：长宽高的大小）；句意是这个房间的尺寸印在图纸上。

senses.title: A measured size
senses.definition: a length, width or height that can be measured
senses.definitionCN: 可以量出来的长、宽或高
senses.example: Check the dimensions before you buy the table.
senses.exampleCN: 买桌子之前先看尺寸。
senses.why: A thing in space always asks to be measured in more than one way.
senses.whyCN: 空间里的东西，总要被不止一种方式量过。

senses.title: One direction in space
senses.definition: one of the directions in which space or a model extends
senses.definitionCN: 空间或模型伸展的某一个方向
senses.example: A line has only one dimension.
senses.exampleCN: 一条线只有一个维度。
senses.why: Counting the directions turns a shape into a number.
senses.whyCN: 把方向数出来，形状就变成了一个数。

senses.title: One side of a matter
senses.definition: one part of a situation that must be considered
senses.definitionCN: 一件事中必须被考虑到的一面
senses.example: The story has a moral dimension as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事还有道德层面。
senses.why: Problems have depth too, and each depth is called a dimension.
senses.whyCN: 问题也有厚度，每一层厚度都叫一个维度。

intro.en: Dimension comes from Latin dimensio, a measuring out, from metiri, to measure.
intro.cn: dimension 来自拉丁语 dimensio（量出），词根是 metiri（测量）。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure land or length.
items.cn: metiri 指丈量土地或长度。

items.en: Dimetiri meant to measure out in full.
items.cn: dimetiri 指完整地量出。

items.en: Dimensio named the result of that measuring.
items.cn: dimensio 指量过之后得到的结果。

items.en: English dimension meant size as measured.
items.cn: 英语 dimension 指量出来的大小。

items.en: Science added the sense of an axis, and common use added the sense of an aspect.
items.cn: 科学添上「坐标轴」的意思，日常用法又添上「方面」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the men- sound, while the meaning group covers size, aspect and extent.
note.cn: 形近组共用 men 这一段音，近义组则覆盖大小、方面与范围。

entries.definition: to become or make smaller
entries.definitionCN: 变小或使变小

entries.definition: to speak or write about briefly
entries.definitionCN: 简短地提到

entries.definition: having a certain number of dimensions
entries.definitionCN: 具有若干维度的

entries.definition: how large or small something is
entries.definitionCN: 某物有多大或多小

entries.definition: one part or feature of a situation
entries.definitionCN: 情况的一个部分或特征

entries.definition: the area or degree something reaches
entries.definitionCN: 某物达到的范围或程度

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from three tape marks on a box to a story with a moral side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从箱子上三道卷尺痕，走到一个有道德层面的故事。

normal.en: Measure, measure, measure: dimension is the count of directions.
normal.cn: 量一次，再量一次：dimension 就是方向的个数。

normal.en: A box needs three numbers; a story needs several sides.
normal.cn: 箱子要三个数，故事要好几面。

normal.en: Add a dimension means one more direction to walk in.
normal.cn: add a dimension 就是多出一个可走的方向。

normal.en: The same word measures a room and a moral question.
normal.cn: 同一个词既量房间，也量道德问题。

normal.en: Metiri is measure, and metre hides inside it.
normal.cn: metiri 是测量，metre 就藏在里面。

abstract.en: Picture a tape measure bent along the edge of a box.
abstract.cn: 想象卷尺贴着箱子边缘拐弯。

abstract.en: Picture three chalk marks at right angles.
abstract.cn: 想象三道互相垂直的粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture a flat drawing that suddenly gains depth.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平面图忽然有了厚度。

examples.en: The sofa fits the dimensions of the room.
examples.cn: 这张沙发与房间的尺寸相合。

examples.en: Time is often called the fourth dimension.
examples.cn: 时间常被称作第四维。

examples.en: Her letter added a personal dimension to the case.
examples.cn: 她的来信为这个案子添了个人层面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dimension 记成「地门神」：门口的地要量一量，量出长宽高，就是尺寸。

root: 来自拉丁语 dimensio，词根 metiri 意为测量，前缀 di- 表示分开、逐项。本义是逐项量出的结果，即长宽高等尺寸；数学与物理把它抽象为「维度」，日常语言又把它引申为事情的「方面」与「规模」。

sensesIntro.en: From a tape laid along a box, to an axis in space, to a side of a question that must be weighed.
sensesIntro.cn: 从贴着箱子的卷尺，到空间中的一根轴，再到一个问题必须被衡量的那一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three tape marks at right angles on one wooden box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木箱上三道互相垂直的卷尺痕。

branches.en: The first sense is the measured size of a thing.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是东西被量出来的大小。

branches.en: The second sense is a direction in space.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是空间里的一个方向。

branches.en: The third sense is a side of a situation.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是事情的一个面。

branches.en: Measuring a box and naming an axis use the same idea.
branches.cn: 量一只箱子与命名一根轴，用的是同一个想法。

branches.en: Depth in space becomes depth in meaning.
branches.cn: 空间里的深度，变成了意思上的深度。

intro.en: Dimension joins a family of measuring words built on the Latin root metiri.
intro.cn: dimension 加入一族表示测量的词，词根是拉丁语 metiri。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin metiri, to measure, seen also in metre and measure.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 metiri（测量），metre 与 measure 里也能看到它。

items.example: The dimension of the box surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这只箱子的尺寸让我们意外。

items.example: Write the dimensions on the label.
The two shapes are dimensionally equal.
items.exampleCN: 这两个形状在尺寸上相等。
贫困是个多层面的问题。

items.meaning: to find the size of something
items.example: Measure the wall before buying paint.
The room is four metres wide.

definition_zh: 尺寸的；量纲的；……维的；立体的；有深度的
definition_en: relating to measurements or dimensions, or having a stated number of dimensions
core_image: 一把游标卡尺同时量出长、宽、高：三个方向都标上刻度
scene: 车间工作台上，工人用卡尺测量一个金属块的长、宽、高。At the workbench the worker measures the length, width and height of a metal block and marks the three dimensional measurements on the drawing.
sceneCN: 这里 dimensional 是「与长宽高有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及物体的长度、宽度与高度）；句意：工人用卡尺量出金属块的长、宽、高，并把三个尺寸标在图纸上。图中可辨识物件：卡尺、金属块、标注长宽高的图纸。

pos.zh: 尺寸的；量纲的；……维的；立体的

derivatives.zh: 维度；尺寸；方面；标注尺寸

senses.title: Relating to length, width and height
senses.definition: of or relating to the measurements that define the size of an object in space
senses.definitionCN: 与界定物体空间大小的测量有关的
senses.example: The dimensional tolerances are given in millimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 尺寸公差以毫米给出。
senses.why: Latin dimetiri is dis- 'apart' plus metiri 'to measure'. A dimension is a measuring-apart, and dimensional means 'belonging to that measuring'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dimetiri 是 dis-“分开”加 metiri“测量”。维度就是“分开地量”，dimensional 意为“属于这种测量的”。

senses.title: Having a stated number of dimensions
senses.definition: used after a number to say how many independent directions a space or figure has
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字后，表示一个空间或图形有几个独立方向
senses.example: The model is a three-dimensional grid of points.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型是一个三维点阵。
senses.why: A point needs one number to locate, a plane needs two, a solid needs three. Adding a dimension means adding one more independent measurement.
senses.whyCN: 定位一个点需要一个数，一个平面需要两个，一个立体需要三个。增加一维就是增加一个独立的测量。

senses.title: Measured in size and shape
senses.definition: describing the accuracy or constancy of the physical size of a manufactured part
senses.definitionCN: 描述制造零件物理尺寸的精确程度或稳定程度
senses.example: Wood is less dimensionally stable than steel.
senses.exampleCN: 木材的尺寸稳定性不如钢。
senses.why: In manufacturing the question is not how many directions but how faithfully the measured size matches the drawing. Dimensional becomes a quality label.
senses.whyCN: 在制造中，问题不是有几个方向，而是实测尺寸多忠实地符合图纸。dimensional 于是成了一个质量标签。

senses.title: Looking solid rather than flat
senses.definition: appearing to have depth as well as height and width, as an image or a film
senses.definitionCN: 像图像或影片那样显得除了高宽之外还有深度
senses.example: The new screen gives a dimensional feel to the drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 新屏幕让这张图有了立体感。
senses.why: The eye reads shading and perspective as extra measurements. A flat picture that supplies them is called dimensional because it restores the third axis.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛把明暗与透视读成额外的测量。一幅提供了这些的平面图像被称为立体的，因为它恢复了第三根轴。

senses.title: Having depth of character
senses.definition: figuratively, having complexity and depth rather than being simple or flat
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义上具有复杂性与深度，而非单薄扁平
senses.example: The novel offers a dimensional portrait of its villain.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说给反派画了一幅有层次的肖像。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the solid object: a flat character has one surface, a dimensional one can be walked around. Depth becomes moral and psychological.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了立体物：扁平角色只有一个面，有维度的角色可以绕着走。深度于是变成道德与心理上的东西。

senses.title: A single aspect of a problem
senses.titleCN: 某一方面的（常与数词连用）
senses.definition: in combinations such as one-dimensional, referring to a single aspect or view of a complex matter
senses.definitionCN: 在 one-dimensional 等组合中，指复杂事情的单一侧面或视角
senses.example: The debate was one-dimensional, ignoring costs entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论只有一个维度，完全忽略了成本。
senses.why: A one-dimensional account has only one axis along which to vary. The word turns a geometric count into a criticism of narrowness.
senses.whyCN: 单一维度的叙述只有一根可以变化的轴。这个词把几何上的计数变成了对狭隘的批评。

senses.title: Checking units by their dimensions
senses.definition: in science, relating to the method of checking equations by comparing the physical dimensions of their terms
senses.definitionCN: 科学中通过比较各项物理量纲来检验方程的方法
senses.example: Dimensional analysis shows the formula must be wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 量纲分析表明这个公式一定有错。
senses.why: Metiri gave the word 'measure'; a dimension is a kind of measure, such as length or time. Dimensional analysis asks whether both sides of an equation measure the same kind of thing.
senses.whyCN: metiri 给出“测量”；量纲是一种测量类别，如长度或时间。量纲分析追问方程两边量的是不是同一类东西。

senses.title: Keeping the same size over time
senses.definition: remaining unchanged in physical size under changes of temperature, moisture or load
senses.definitionCN: 在温度、湿度或载荷变化下物理尺寸保持不变
senses.example: The composite is dimensionally stable under heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种复合材料受热时尺寸稳定。
senses.why: Here dimension means the measured size itself. A material that does not grow or shrink has kept its measurements, so it is dimensionally stable.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 dimension 指被量出的尺寸本身。不胀不缩的材料守住了它的测量值，所以是尺寸稳定的。

intro.en: Dimensional is dimension plus -al. Dimension comes from Latin dimensio, a noun from dimetiri 'to measure out', built on metiri 'to measure'. The adjective is a later English formation, and its technical senses grew in mathematics, engineering and criticism.
intro.cn: dimensional 是 dimension 加 -al。dimension 来自拉丁 dimensio，由 dimetiri“量出”而来，其词根是 metiri“测量”。形容词是较晚的英语构造，其技术义在数学、工程与文艺批评中各自生长。

items.en: The root *me- meant 'to measure'. It gives Latin metiri, English meal in the old sense of 'measured portion', and the Greek metron behind metre and symmetry.
items.cn: 词根 *me- 意为“测量”。它给出拉丁 metiri、英语 meal（古义“一份量”），以及 metre 与 symmetry 背后的希腊 metron。

items.en: Metiri meant 'to measure'. With dis- it became dimetiri, 'to measure out, to mark off', used by Roman land surveyors laying out plots.
items.cn: metiri 意为“测量”。加 dis- 成为 dimetiri“量出、划出”，罗马土地测量员用它来划分地块。

items.en: The noun dimensio named a measuring-out and then the measure itself. Latin used it for the size of a body and for the parts of a geometric figure.
items.cn: 名词 dimensio 指量出的动作，后指量出的结果。拉丁语用它指物体的大小与几何图形的各部分。

items.en: English dimension arrives in the 16th century from French, first as 'measurement, size'. The geometric sense of an axis of space is fixed in the 17th century.
items.cn: 英语 dimension 于 16 世纪从法语进入，初义为“测量、大小”。空间轴线的几何义在 17 世纪固定。

items.en: The adjective dimensional appears in the 18th century, and compounds such as three-dimensional spread with geometry teaching and later with printing and film.
items.cn: 形容词 dimensional 出现于 18 世纪，three-dimensional 等复合词随几何教学传播，后又随印刷与电影扩散。

items.en: Dimensional analysis enters physics in the 19th century; dimensional stability enters engineering; the figurative 'flat or full character' use enters criticism in the 20th.
items.cn: 量纲分析在 19 世纪进入物理学；尺寸稳定性进入工程学；比喻性的“扁平或有层次的角色”用法在 20 世纪进入文艺批评。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun, its negation and the adverb. The meaning group contrasts dimensions with mere size, with spatial extent and with measurement generally.
note.cn: 形近组区分名词、其否定形式与副词；词义组把“维度”与单纯的“大小”“空间范围”“一般测量”区分开。

entries.definition: a measurement in space, an aspect of a situation, or a level of a problem. The adjective is built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 空间中的测量、情境的一面，或问题的一个层面。形容词由它构成。

entries.definition: having no physical units, as a pure ratio. It is the opposite technical pole from dimensional.
entries.definitionCN: 没有物理单位的，如纯比值。它是在技术义上与 dimensional 相反的一端。

entries.definition: in terms of dimensions or measurements. The adverb modifies a verb; the adjective modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 就维度或尺寸而言。副词修饰动词，形容词修饰名词。

entries.definition: relating to space and the position of things in it. It names the field, while dimensional names the measurements within it.
entries.definitionCN: 与空间及事物在其中的位置有关的。它指领域，而 dimensional 指领域内的度量。

entries.definition: relating to the properties of shapes. A geometric figure has dimensionality, but a dimensional report also includes tolerances.
entries.definitionCN: 与图形性质有关的。几何图形有维度，而尺寸报告还包含公差。

entries.definition: relating to measurement by volume. It specifies what is measured, whereas dimensional only says that measuring is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 与按体积测量有关的。它指明量的是什么，而 dimensional 只说涉及测量。

entries.definition: capable of being measured. A dimensional claim presupposes that something measurable exists.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被测量的。尺寸方面的论断预设了有可测之物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from the measuring root met-, then attach the three counts that matter: length, width, height.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从测量词根 met- 搭起这个词，再挂上真正重要的三个数：长、宽、高。

normal.en: See di- + metiri: measuring apart, one axis at a time.
normal.cn: 看见 di- 加 metiri：一根轴一根轴地分开量。

normal.en: Count the numbers needed to locate a point: one, two, three. That count is the dimension.
normal.cn: 数一数定位一个点需要几个数：一个、两个、三个。这个数目就是维数。

normal.en: In a workshop, dimensional means the part matches the drawing in size.
normal.cn: 在车间里，dimensional 指零件的尺寸符合图纸。

normal.en: Link three-dimensional with film: the screen adds a third axis to a flat picture.
normal.cn: 把 three-dimensional 连到电影：屏幕给平面图像加上了第三根轴。

normal.en: Remember one-dimensional as an insult: only one axis, so no breadth of view.
normal.cn: 记住 one-dimensional 是贬义：只有一根轴，因而没有视野的宽度。

abstract.en: Hold the image of a caliper closing on a block: every sense of the word comes from that closing.
abstract.cn: 抓住卡尺夹住金属块的意象：这个词的每个义项都来自那一次夹合。

abstract.en: Treat dimensions as questions you can ask of a thing: how long, how wide, how deep, how complex.
abstract.cn: 把维度当作可以问一件事的问题：多长、多宽、多深、多复杂。

abstract.en: Notice that a dimension is not a thing but a way of measuring; the adjective always implies a frame.
abstract.cn: 注意维度不是东西，而是测量的方式；这个形容词总是隐含着一个参照框架。

examples.en: The painter achieves a dimensional effect with light and shadow alone.
examples.cn: 这位画家仅凭光影就取得了立体效果。

examples.en: Dimensional analysis caught the error before the experiment began.
examples.cn: 量纲分析在实验开始前就抓到了错误。

examples.en: The alloy stays dimensionally stable at high temperatures.
examples.cn: 这种合金在高温下尺寸保持稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地门神哪儿”：量地、量门、量神龛，哪儿都要量尺寸——dimensional 就是尺寸与维度的。

root: 拉丁语 metiri“测量”，加 dis- 成 dimetiri“量出、划出”，名词 dimensio“量出的结果、大小”；经法语进入英语作 dimension，再加形容词后缀 -al 构成 dimensional。同根词有 metre、measure、symmetry（希腊同源 metron）。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of dimensional comes from one act: measuring out. The word asks how many independent measurements a thing needs, or how faithfully its measured size holds. From that single question it reaches geometry, engineering tolerance, the illusion of depth on a flat screen, and finally the metaphor of a character or argument that has more than one side.
sensesIntro.cn: dimensional 的每个义项都来自同一个动作：量出。这个词追问一件事需要几个独立的测量，或它被量出的尺寸有多可靠。从这一个问题出发，它伸到几何、工程公差、平面屏幕上的深度错觉，最后到“角色或论点不止一面”的比喻。

core.en: Measured out: assigning numbers along independent axes.
core.cn: 量出：沿着彼此独立的轴赋予数值。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: size, tolerance and stability of a real object.
branches.cn: 测量：真实物体的尺寸、公差与稳定性。

branches.en: GEOMETRY AND PHYSICS: how many axes, and whether units balance.
branches.cn: 几何与物理：有几根轴，以及单位是否配平。

branches.en: ILLUSION: a flat image restored to three axes.
branches.cn: 错觉：平面图像被恢复成三根轴。

branches.en: CHARACTER: a person or work that can be walked around.
branches.cn: 性格：可以绕着看的人或作品。

branches.en: NARROW VIEW: a complex matter reduced to one aspect.
branches.cn: 狭窄视角：复杂之事被缩到一面。

intro.en: Dimensional is a noun plus -al, and the noun itself is a prefixed form of the measuring root. The items trace that root through English and show the negative and abstract forms built on dimension.
intro.cn: dimensional 是名词加 -al，名词本身又是测量词根加前缀的形式。下列条目追踪这个词根在英语中的走向，并展示由 dimension 构成的否定与抽象形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb of measuring and its two derived nouns. They explain why 'dimension' can mean both a line on a drawing and a facet of a story.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出测量的动词及其两个派生名词。它们解释了为什么 dimension 既能指图纸上的一条标注，也能指故事的一个侧面。

items.example: The dimensional error was under a tenth of a millimetre.
items.exampleCN: 尺寸误差不到十分之一毫米。

items.example: Cost is only one dimension of the problem.
items.exampleCN: 成本只是这个问题的一个方面。

items.meaning: the number or quality of dimensions

items.example: The two parts are dimensionally identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两个零件在尺寸上完全相同。

items.meaning: to determine size; a size determined
a unit of length; poetic measure
items.example: The room is four metres long.

items.meaning: the same measure on both sides; balance
items.example: The building's symmetry pleases the eye.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑的对称令人悦目。

items.example: The immense plain stretched to the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 巨大的平原一直延伸到地平线。

latinEntries.meaning: to measure out, to mark off

definition_zh: 减少；缩小；削弱；贬低；减轻
definition_en: to become or make smaller, weaker, or less important
core_image: 一块方糖在水里越缩越小
scene: 烛台上的蜡烛越烧越短，墙上的影子慢慢拉长。 As the candle burned shorter, the light on the wall diminished.
sceneCN: 这里 diminish 是「变小、减弱」（第 5 个义项：声音或光减弱）；句意：随着蜡烛越烧越短，墙上的光逐渐减弱。

senses.title: Become smaller or less
senses.definition: to become smaller in size, amount, or number
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或数目上变小
senses.example: The lake diminished over the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖在夏天渐渐变小。
senses.why: The verb is a merger of two old words built on Latin minuere 'make small'. The intransitive sense, recorded in the 1510s, lets the thing itself grow less without an agent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由两个建立在拉丁语 minuere“使变小”的古词合并而成。1510 年代记录的不及物义，让事物自身变少，无需施动者。

senses.title: Make something smaller
senses.definition: to reduce the size or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 减小某物的大小或数量
senses.example: The drug diminishes appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药会降低食欲。
senses.why: With a direct object the same root becomes transitive: an outside cause makes the thing less. English inherited both the transitive and intransitive patterns from its two source verbs.
senses.whyCN: 带直接宾语时，同一词根转为及物：外部原因使事物变少。英语从两个来源动词继承及物与不及物两种模式。

senses.title: Reduce power or importance
senses.definition: to make someone or something less powerful or important
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物权力更小、重要性更低
senses.example: The scandal diminished his authority.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻削弱了他的权威。
senses.why: The mid-15c sense was 'lower in power, importance, or estimation'. Power is treated as a quantity that can be made smaller, like a pile of grain.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期的义项是“降低权力、重要性或评价”。权力被当作一种可以变小的量，像一堆谷物。

senses.title: Reduce value or worth
senses.definition: to make something worth less, especially money or assets
senses.definitionCN: 使某物价值更低，尤指金钱或资产
senses.example: Inflation diminishes savings.
senses.exampleCN: 通货膨胀使储蓄贬值。
senses.why: Value is measured on a scale, and a smaller position on the scale is a diminished value. The word's measuring origin survives in this economic use.
senses.whyCN: 价值是在尺度上度量的，尺度上的位置更小就是价值被降低。这个词的测量出身在经济用法中保留下来。

senses.title: Fade in strength
senses.definition: to become weaker in sound, light, or force
senses.definitionCN: 声音、光线或力量变弱
senses.example: The noise diminished as the train left.
senses.exampleCN: 火车远去，噪声逐渐减弱。
senses.why: A sound has no fixed size, but it has intensity. Diminish treats intensity as an amount that can shrink until the sound disappears.
senses.whyCN: 声音没有固定大小，但有强度。diminish 把强度当作可以缩小、直到声音消失的量。

senses.title: Belittle a person
senses.definition: to make a person seem less important or valuable
senses.definitionCN: 使某人显得不那么重要或有价值
senses.example: He never missed a chance to diminish her.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不放过贬低她的机会。
senses.why: The same act of lowering can be applied to a person's standing. To diminish someone is to reduce their perceived size in the eyes of others.
senses.whyCN: 同一种“降低”可以施加于人的地位。贬低某人，就是缩小他在别人眼中的分量。

senses.title: Lessen pain or risk
senses.definition: to reduce the intensity of pain, danger, or a bad effect
senses.definitionCN: 降低痛苦、危险或不良影响的强度
senses.example: Proper care diminishes the risk of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 适当护理能降低感染风险。
senses.why: Risk and pain are quantities of harm. Diminish is the neutral verb for making them smaller; it does not remove them entirely, only lowers the amount.
senses.whyCN: 风险与痛苦是“伤害的量”。diminish 是使它们变小的中性动词；它不彻底消除，只降低数量。

senses.title: Reduce a musical interval
senses.definition: in music, to lower an interval by a semitone, producing a diminished chord or interval
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中把音程缩小半音，形成减音程或减和弦
senses.example: The chord uses a diminished fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个和弦用了减五度。
senses.why: Music borrowed the visual idea of shrinking: an interval that is one semitone smaller than its natural form is 'diminished', as if a measured length were cut short.
senses.whyCN: 音乐借用了“缩小”的视觉意象：比自然形式小一个半音的音程被称为“减的”，仿佛一段被截短的长度。

senses.title: Diminishing returns
senses.definition: in economics, the phrase for the point where extra effort yields less and less benefit
senses.definitionCN: 经济学用语，指额外投入带来的收益越来越少
senses.example: Each extra hour brings diminishing returns.
senses.exampleCN: 每多投入一小时，收益都在递减。
senses.why: The phrase treats benefit as a quantity that shrinks with each additional unit of effort. Diminish names the direction of the curve, not a one-time loss.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把收益当作随每增加一单位投入而缩小的量。diminish 指曲线的走向，而非一次性损失。

intro.en: Diminish is a double heritage: two Old French verbs, both from Latin words for 'make small', merged into one English verb in the early 15th century.
intro.cn: diminish 是双重遗产：两个古法语动词都来自拉丁语“使变小”，在 15 世纪初合并成一个英语动词。

items.en: diminishen appears as a merger of two obsolete verbs, diminue and minish.
items.cn: diminishen 出现，是两个已废弃动词 diminue 与 minish 的合并。

items.en: diminue comes from Old French diminuer and Latin diminuere 'break into small pieces', a variant of deminuere 'lessen'.
items.cn: diminue 来自古法语 diminuer 与拉丁语 diminuere“打碎成小块”，后者是 deminuere“减少”的变体。

items.en: minish comes from Old French menuisier and Latin minuere 'make small'.
items.cn: minish 来自古法语 menuisier 与拉丁语 minuere“使变小”。

items.en: deminuere = de- 'completely' + minuere 'make small', from PIE *mei- 'small'.
items.cn: deminuere = de-“完全”+ minuere“使变小”，源自原始印欧语 *mei-“小”。

items.en: The sense 'lower in power, importance, or estimation' appears.
items.cn: “降低权力、重要性或评价”的义项出现。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'grow less, become or appear smaller' is recorded.
items.cn: 不及物义“变少、变小或显得更小”被记录。

note.en: The first group is about shared beginnings or endings; the second is about verbs that also make something less.
note.cn: 第一组看相同的词首或词尾，第二组看同样使某物变少的动词。

entries.definition: a measurable direction or aspect. It shares the dimi- opening but comes from metiri 'measure'.
entries.definitionCN: 可测的方向或方面。同样以 dimi- 开头，但来自 metiri“测量”。

entries.definition: extremely small; also a word form expressing smallness. It comes from the same minuere family.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；也指表示“小”的词形。它出自同一个 minuere 词族。

entries.definition: to destroy a building completely. It rhymes in -ish but comes from demoliri, not minuere.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底拆毁建筑。词尾 -ish 押韵，但来自 demoliri，而非 minuere。

entries.definition: to become or make less in number or size. It is the most neutral partner of diminish.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或大小上变少。它是最中性的 diminish 近义词。

entries.definition: to make something smaller, often deliberately. It stresses an agent and a method.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变小，常为有意为之。它强调施动者与方法。

entries.definition: to make pain, risk, or an effect smaller. It is close to diminish but usually takes an abstract object.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻痛苦、风险或影响。它接近 diminish，但常接抽象宾语。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the two merged verbs, the Latin minuere 'make small', the 1510s intransitive sense, and musical diminished intervals.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：两个合并的动词、拉丁语 minuere“使变小”、1510 年代的不及物义，以及音乐中的减音程。

normal.en: Two Old French verbs, diminue and minish, both meant 'make small'. English merged them into diminish.
normal.cn: 两个古法语动词 diminue 与 minish 都表示“使变小”。英语把它们合并成 diminish。

normal.en: The Latin core is minuere 'make small'; minimum and minor belong to the same smallness family.
normal.cn: 拉丁核心是 minuere“使变小”；minimum 与 minor 属于同一个“小”的词族。

normal.en: Intransitive use came in the 1510s: a lake can diminish by itself, without anyone shrinking it.
normal.cn: 不及物用法出现于 1510 年代：湖泊可以自己变小，无需别人去缩。

normal.en: Power and value are treated as amounts: to diminish someone is to lower their position on a scale.
normal.cn: 权力与价值被当作数量：贬低某人就是降低他在尺度上的位置。

normal.en: A diminished chord is one semitone 'cut short', the same shrinking image applied to sound.
normal.cn: 减和弦就是被“截短”一个半音，同一个缩小意象用在声音上。

abstract.en: Diminish is quantitative: it lowers an amount without asking whether the remainder is still enough.
abstract.cn: diminish 是量化的：它降低数量，却不问剩下的是否仍然够用。

abstract.en: The same verb covers physical shrinkage, social standing, value, and intensity: all are amounts on some scale.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词覆盖物理缩小、社会地位、价值与强度：它们都是某种尺度上的量。

abstract.en: Belittling is shrinking a person in other minds, which shows how easily a measuring word becomes a moral one.
abstract.cn: 贬低就是在他人心中缩小一个人，可见一个测量词多么容易变成道德词。

examples.en: The lake diminished over the summer.
examples.cn: 这个湖在夏天渐渐变小。

examples.en: The drug diminishes appetite.
examples.cn: 这种药会降低食欲。

examples.en: Each extra hour brings diminishing returns.
examples.cn: 每多投入一小时，收益都在递减。

dict_mnemonic.text: “低迷你”——低到迷你尺寸 → diminish 变小、减少

root: 拉丁语 deminuere / minuere“使变小”，由 de-“完全”+ minuere“变小”构成；同族有 minimum、minor。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of diminish, all built on one image: a quantity shrinking. The quantity can be size, power, value, sound, pain, or benefit.
sensesIntro.cn: diminish 的九个义项都建立在一个意象上：数量缩小。这个量可以是大小、权力、价值、声音、痛苦或收益。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sugar cube shrinking smaller and smaller in water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块方糖在水里越缩越小。

branches.en: SIZE: the core physical sense, intransitive or transitive.
branches.cn: 大小：核心的物理义，可及物也可不及物。

branches.en: STATUS AND VALUE: power and worth are amounts on a social or economic scale.
branches.cn: 地位与价值：权力与价值是社会或经济尺度上的量。

branches.en: FORCE AND HARM: sound fades and pain or risk is lowered.
branches.cn: 力量与伤害：声音减弱，痛苦或风险被降低。

branches.en: BELITTLE: the same lowering is applied to a person's standing.
branches.cn: 贬低：同一种降低施加于人的地位。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND PHRASE: music cuts an interval short; economics names a curve of shrinking benefit.
branches.cn: 技术与短语：音乐把音程截短；经济学命名一条收益缩小的曲线。

intro.en: Diminish is a verb from Latin minuere. English adds -ed, -ing, -tion, and -ive, and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: diminish 是来自拉丁语 minuere 的动词。英语加 -ed、-ing、-tion、-ive，以及否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: Latin minuere 'make small' yields minutus 'small' and the noun minuere family behind minimum, minor, and minute. Deminuere adds de- 'completely'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minuere“使变小”生成 minutus“小的”，以及 minimum、minor、minute 背后的词族。Deminuere 加上 de-“完全”。

items.meaning: made smaller or weaker; also, a musical interval reduced by a semitone
items.meaningCN: 减少的；减弱的；（音乐）减音程的

items.meaning: becoming less; often used in 'diminishing returns'
items.meaningCN: 逐渐减少的；“收益递减”常用

items.meaning: a reduction in size, amount, or importance
very small; a word form that expresses smallness
the act or result of reducing something
items.meaningCN: 减少；削弱（-ment 构成名词）

items.meaning: a musical direction to grow quieter
items.meaningCN: 渐弱（音乐术语，源自拉丁语“减少”）

items.meaning: in a way that becomes less and less

latinEntries.meaning: to break into small pieces; lessen

definition_zh: 恐龙
definition_en: a very large animal that lived long ago and is now extinct
core_image: 博物馆里一具高大的恐龙骨架，孩子在它脚下仰头看
scene: 博物馆里一具高大的恐龙骨架，孩子在它脚下仰头看。A dinosaur skeleton stands in the museum hall.
sceneCN: 这里 dinosaur 是「恐龙」（第 01 个义项）；句意是博物馆大厅里立着一具恐龙骨架。

senses.title: A large extinct animal of the distant past
senses.definition: a large animal with four legs and a long tail that lived millions of years ago and is now extinct
senses.definitionCN: 数百万年前生活、如今已灭绝的大型四足长尾动物
senses.example: A dinosaur skeleton stands in the museum hall.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆大厅里立着一具恐龙骨架。
senses.why: Greek deinos, terrible, plus sauros, lizard, gave dinosaur, the "terrible lizard" named by a Victorian scientist for the giant fossil bones.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 deinos（可怕的）加 sauros（蜥蜴）构成 dinosaur，维多利亚时代的学者见到巨大化石，把它命名为「可怕的蜥蜴」。

senses.title: Someone or something hopelessly out of date
senses.definition: a person or thing that is old-fashioned and cannot adapt
senses.definitionCN: 跟不上时代、无法适应的人或事物
senses.example: The old typewriter is a dinosaur in a modern office.
senses.exampleCN: 在现代办公室里，那台旧打字机是个老古董。
senses.why: Dinosaurs died out while the world changed, so the name became a metaphor for anything that cannot keep up and disappears.
senses.whyCN: 恐龙在世界改变时灭绝了，这个名字就被用来比喻跟不上变化、终将消失的事物。

intro.en: The history of dinosaur is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: dinosaur 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Deinos meant terrible or fearful.
items.cn: 希腊语 deinos 意为「可怕的」。

items.en: Sauros meant a lizard.
items.cn: 希腊语 sauros 意为「蜥蜴」。

items.en: Dinosaur means terrible lizard.
items.cn: dinosaur 意为「可怕的蜥蜴」。

items.en: The name spread with fossil finds.
items.cn: 这个名字随化石发现而传播。

items.en: Dinosaur also means something outdated.
items.cn: 现代英语中它还指过时的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in form, root or spelling; the near-meaning group collects words from the same everyday field.

intro.en: Dioxide joins Greek di- twice to oxide, a French coinage from oxygène and acide, whose oxy- comes from Greek oxys, sharp or acid.
intro.cn: dioxide 把希腊语 di-（二）与 oxide 拼在一起；oxide 是法语用 oxygène 与 acide 造的词，其中 oxy- 来自希腊语 oxys（尖的、酸的）。

items.en: Di- meant twice.
items.cn: di- 意为两次。

items.en: Oxys meant sharp or acid.
items.cn: oxys 意为尖的、酸的。

items.en: Genes meant born or producing.
items.cn: genes 意为产生的。

items.en: French coined oxide from oxygène and acide.
items.cn: 十八世纪法语用 oxygène 与 acide 造出 oxide。

items.en: Dioxide named a compound with two oxygens.
items.cn: 十九世纪 dioxide 指含两个氧的化合物。

items.en: Carbon dioxide became the headline gas.
items.cn: 二十世纪二氧化碳成了头条气体。

definition_zh: 浸；蘸；下降；凹陷处
definition_en: to put something briefly into liquid, or to go down and then up again
core_image: 一片面包被捏着边角，往热汤里按下去又提起来
scene: 他把面包掰开，捏着一角很快按进汤里。She dipped her hand in the cold stream.
sceneCN: 这里 dipped 指「浸入」（第 1 个义项：短时间放进液体里）；句意是她把手浸进冰凉的小溪。

senses.title: To put in liquid briefly
senses.definition: to lower something into liquid for a short moment
senses.definitionCN: 把东西放进液体里很短一会儿
senses.example: She dipped her hand in the cold stream.
senses.exampleCN: 她把手浸进冰凉的小溪。
senses.why: The hand goes down and comes back before the water can hold it.
senses.whyCN: 手沉下去又提起来，水还没来得及留住它。

senses.title: To fall and rise again
senses.definition: to go down for a while, as a number or a path does
senses.definitionCN: 像数字或道路那样暂时往下走
senses.example: Sales dipped below last year's level.
senses.exampleCN: 销量降到了去年的水平以下。
senses.why: The line on the chart bends down, then finds its way back.
senses.whyCN: 图上的线往下一沉，随后又找回自己。

senses.title: A hollow in the ground
senses.definition: a place where the surface goes down and then up
senses.definitionCN: 表面先往下再往上的一处地方
senses.example: A small dip in the road holds water after rain.
senses.exampleCN: 路上一个小坑雨后积着水。
senses.why: The motion of dipping becomes a shape in the land.
senses.whyCN: 「往下一沉」的动作，变成了地面上的一个形状。

intro.en: Dip comes from Old English dyppan, a Germanic verb for putting something into water.
intro.cn: dip 来自古英语 dyppan，是日耳曼语中表示「把东西放进水里」的动词。

items.en: A root dup- linked dipping with depth.
items.cn: 词根 dup- 把「浸」与「深」连在一起。

items.en: Dyppan meant to baptise or to plunge something in.
items.cn: dyppan 指施洗，或把东西按进水里。

items.en: Dippen widened to any short plunge into liquid.
items.cn: dippen 扩展到任何短时间的入水。

items.en: The noun named a hollow and a short swim.
items.cn: 名词义开始指凹坑与短暂的游泳。

items.en: Dipping also describes numbers falling for a while.
items.cn: dip 还用来形容数字暂时下滑。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the d- and short vowel, while the meaning group covers plunging, soaking and sinking.
note.cn: 形近组共用短元音与 d 开头，近义组则覆盖猛插、浸泡与下沉。

entries.definition: reaching far down from the top

entries.definition: a long-handled cup for scooping liquid

entries.definition: a continuing loud noise
entries.definitionCN: 持续不断的响声

entries.definition: to push suddenly and deeply into something
entries.definitionCN: 猛地深深插进去

entries.definition: to cover completely with liquid
entries.definitionCN: 用液体完全盖住

entries.definition: to go down slowly below a surface
entries.definitionCN: 慢慢沉到表面之下

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从按进汤里的面包开始，最后落到一个积着雨水的小坑。

normal.cn: dip in 是快的一下，soak 是长时间泡。

normal.en: Take a dip means the whole body gets the treatment.
normal.cn: take a dip 是说整个人都进去泡一泡。

normal.en: A dip in sales is a hollow on a chart.
normal.cn: 销量的 dip，是图表上的一个凹口。

normal.en: Dip into a book, not through it.

abstract.en: Picture bread going under soup for one second.
abstract.cn: 想象面包在汤里沉了一秒。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifting dark liquid from a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子从罐里舀起深色的液体。

abstract.en: Picture a shallow hollow shining after rain.

examples.cn: 他把刷子蘸进颜料里。

examples.en: There is a dip in the path just before the gate.

sensesIntro.en: From a quick plunge of bread into soup, to a falling line, to the hollow that line leaves in the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 从面包在汤里的一沉，到一条下落的线，再到那条线在地面上留下的凹坑。

branches.en: The first sense is the short plunge into liquid.

branches.en: The second sense moves the plunge onto numbers.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这一沉挪到数字上。

branches.en: The third sense freezes the motion into ground.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这个动作冻成了地面。

branches.en: Both describe a short fall and a return.
branches.cn: 两者都描述短暂的下落与回返。

branches.en: A dip in a figure and a dip in a road look the same on paper.
branches.cn: 数字的下滑与路面的凹陷，画在纸上一个样。

intro.cn: dip 长出一小族词，涉及勺具、工具与潜水的水鸟。

definition_zh: 外交；外交实务；外交手腕；外交界；（喻）交际策略
definition_en: the conduct of relations between states through negotiation and contact, and the skill of managing such relations without giving offence
core_image: 长桌两侧各坐一人，桌上摊着几张对折的文书，桌下两双脚都没有后退
scene: 长桌两侧各坐一人，桌上摊着几张对折的文书，侍者退到门边，谁也没有先起身。Quiet diplomacy kept the two delegations talking through the winter.
sceneCN: 这里 diplomacy 指「以持续谈判与往来处理国家间关系的实务」（第 1 个义项：通过接触而非武力处理对外关系的方式）；句意为静默外交让两个代表团在整个冬天都保持对话。图中可辨识物件：长桌、对折的文书、两侧的座椅、退到门边的侍者。

pos.zh: 外交；外交实务；外交手腕；外交界（不可数；指具体的外交活动时可数，复数 diplomacies）

forms.label: 复数（指多国的外交活动）

derivatives.zh: 外交官（由 diplomatic 逆构而来，语义由「外交的」收窄为执行外交的人）
